model_annotation: This plot illustrates three policy uncertainty indices over time: "Wirtschaftspolitik insgesamt" (overall economic policy), "Finanzpolitik" (financial policy), and "Handelspolitik" (trade policy). The x-axis represents time, spanning from 2016 to approximately mid-2025, with major tick labels at 2016, 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024 on a linear scale. The left y-axis is labeled "Index" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1,000, with tick intervals of 100, and applies to the first two series. The right y-axis is also labeled "Index" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 9,000, with tick intervals of 1,000, and applies to the trade policy series. The black solid line representing "Wirtschaftspolitik insgesamt" begins near 75 in 2016, fluctuates between roughly 50 and 150 through 2018 and 2019, then spikes sharply around early 2020 to a peak of approximately 500, before declining back to around 100–150 through 2021 and remaining in the range of roughly 80–130 from 2022 through 2024, after which it rises steeply at the end of the series to approximately 700–850. The blue solid line representing "Finanzpolitik" starts near 10 in 2016, rises to fluctuate between approximately 50 and 200 during 2017–2019, peaks around 300 in early 2020 coinciding with the overall economic policy spike, then settles to roughly 80–150 through 2021–2024, before surging sharply at the end of the series to approximately 800–900. The pink/mauve solid line representing "Handelspolitik" (mapped to the right y-axis) begins near 0 in 2016, rises to fluctuate between roughly 500 and 2,000 on the right scale during 2017–2019, drops back toward near 0 around 2020, and remains close to 0 through most of 2021–2024, before exhibiting a dramatic spike at the very end of the series reaching approximately 8,000–9,000 on the right y-axis.
